key_terms: A plugin in a supported application, such as Hive, that observes operations and publishes metadata notifications to Atlas.
A metadata change message, typically delivered through Kafka, that Atlas consumes to update its graph.
Submitting entities directly to Atlas's REST API. It records explicit metadata and does not prove a hook observed a real execution.
Creating or updating an entity by its qualifiedName so a retried request updates the same asset instead of creating a duplicate.
A record of who or what produced a metadata entry and how, which distinguishes hook observations from manual API submissions.

worked_examples.title: Look up an entity by its unique name
worked_examples.interpretation: qualifiedName is the identity Atlas uses to decide whether a submission creates a new entity or updates an existing one. Submitting the same payload twice should return the same GUID both times, which makes a retried ingestion safe. If a retry creates a second entity, the qualifiedName changed between runs, often because it embedded a timestamp or a run ID instead of a stable logical name.

worked_examples.title: Compare GUIDs across a deliberate retry
worked_examples.interpretation: The dictionaries stand in for the entity_guids field that two check receipts produce, one before and one after a repeated apply. Comparing them key by key separates an idempotent retry from a duplicate. A partially failed bulk request is the harder case: some entities may exist and others not, so read back every expected key before resubmitting rather than assuming nothing was written.

evidence: Complete real Atlas REST payload/client route with default local server omitted. Native compatible server preparation and actual API/graph/index/lifecycle acceptance are explicit separate work, never simulated execution.
